intent: "What came back overnight, and what needs answering first?" — filterable by meaning, channel, owner, campaign and how long each has been waiting, ordered by what is most overdue
before_repeating: nothing at stake; page with the returned cursor

input_schema.title: conversation.list input
input_schema.description: One page of conversation threads: one person's across the account when a person is named, otherwise one campaign's. A person's threads need no campaign: a read on request names none, and a work item's campaign is context only.

external_id.description: The provider's own identifier, given to link a campaign for the first time. Later calls work by the pin.

limit.description: At most this many threads on the page. Required: absence is not a default, and a page may come back shorter.

offset.description: Where the page starts in the provider's own order: 0 for the first page, then the previous page's `offset` plus the number of items it returned.

since.description: Only threads that moved at or after this moment.

source.description: `inbound`: only threads the other side wrote into. `all`: every thread. Required, because which of the two a caller meant is not something to guess.

thread_channel.description: Only threads on this channel, in the words a thread's own `channel` is said in. A filter on the threads, never a channel the call consumes: a list reaches nobody.

category.description: Only threads filed under this category of the provider's, by the identifier the reads report under `vendor.category.id`.

contacts.description: The work item's person, present only when the work item names one.

external_ids.description: Only this plugin's own pins reach it. A person with no pin here is one the provider has never been told about by this installation.
Only this plugin's own pins reach it, so another provider's identifier is never visible here.

external_id.description: The provider's identifier for the thread, the one `conversation.get` reads by.

subject.description: The thread's subject, or null where the channel has none.

preview.description: The start of the latest message as the provider shows it, at most 500 characters; null when the provider shows none.

last_activity_at.description: When the thread last moved, in UTC. The page is ordered by it, most recent first.

unread.description: Whether the provider holds the thread as unread.

contact.description: The person on the thread as the provider names them: its identifier, null when the provider no longer holds the person, and a display name. Null when the thread names nobody.

campaign_external_id.description: The provider's identifier for the campaign the thread belongs to, or null.

has_meeting_intent.description: The provider's own judgement that the thread asks for a meeting, or null when it makes none.

vendor.description: The provider's own words about the thread. A closed list, so no address or message text can travel here.

has_more.description: Whether the provider holds more threads after this page.

ordering.description: The provider's own order, the one `offset` counts in: the thread that moved last first.

campaign.description: The provider's identifier for the campaign whose threads this read listed, returned only when the read made the first link. It is never the person's.

failure_codes.when: No provider identifier is pinned for this person, and a read creates nobody.
The provider account's plan or role does not include this capability, so no call by this account can answer it.
The provider's answer was larger than this installation lets a plugin read from a program (`Plugins:Exec:OutputBytes`), so it was cut off; asking again would cut it the same way.
The vendor tool refused the call or never started, so nothing the operation asks for was ever attempted. Repeating it runs the same broken call.
The plugin's own credential does not let it read conversations for this account.
The provider refused the read for now and it may be asked again.
The provider could not be reached, or answered with a failure on its own side.
The provider was called and no answer arrived. A read changes nothing and costs nothing, so the next attempt simply asks again.

The provider refused this call for a reason outside the work item — the account's money or plan, an allowance it counts, a credential it no longer accepts, a channel disconnected or paused — and did nothing for it. The failure's block says what is blocked, why and where a person clears it; a repeat once it clears is a first act. It is said even where the operation also declares an older code for the condition, which then stands for an answer the plugin cannot read as a block.

conformance: A page holds at most `limit` threads, starting at `offset` in the provider's own order, and `has_more` says whether more follow.

A page may come back short of `limit` with `has_more: true`: the plugin stops before the result would pass 768 KiB, counted as the runtime counts it (six bytes for DEL, for every character outside ASCII and for each of `<`, `>`, `&`, `'`, `"`, `+` and the backtick, twelve for one outside the Basic Multilingual Plane).
The next page starts at `offset` plus the number of items this page returned, never at `offset + limit`.
Threads come most recent activity first, which `vendor.ordering` states. The order is not a queue of what to answer: what needs answering first is a judgement this read does not make.
With a person, the page is that person's threads across the account, and the campaign is context only; without one, it is the campaign's threads.
`thread_channel` and `category` keep only the threads on that channel and filed under that category, and the provider applies them before it pages, so `offset` counts the threads that pass them.
A person with no provider identifier pinned fails `contact_not_linked`, and nothing is called: a read creates nobody.
A preview is at most 500 characters, cut where a character ends.
No address appears anywhere in the result: a thread's person is their identifier and the name the provider shows.
A read pins no person: the only identifier it may return under `external_ids` is the campaign's, and only when it made the first link.
